summary: This work proposes suppressing leakage errors in quantum gates by applying small static offsets to tunable system parameters, without modifying control pulse shapes or adding time overhead. Numerical validation on superconducting transmon qubits demonstrates high-fidelity single-qubit gates (NOT and Hadamard reaching 99.98% and 99.92%), two-qubit iSWAP gates (99.87%), multi-level state transfer (99.91%), and cooperative suppression of leakage and ZZ crosstalk via integration with geometric trajectory correction.
motivation: Leakage into higher energy levels fundamentally limits gate fidelity in superconducting qubits and other platforms; existing suppression methods require modified pulse shapes (DRAG, GRAPE) or hardware overhead, motivating a simpler approach compatible with standard control frameworks.
method: The approach identifies a unitary transformation $A(\delta p_i)$ whose boundary conditions enforce leakage suppression via static parameter offsets to coupling strength ($\delta\Omega$ or $\delta g_{12}$), detuning ($\delta\Delta$), and phase ($\delta\phi$). For transmon qubits, optimal offsets are determined by minimizing gate infidelity through numerical optimization while satisfying the Magnus expansion constraint that leakage Hamiltonian contributions vanish in the transformed frame.
result: For single-qubit gates with $\kappa_1 = \kappa_\phi = 2\pi \times 2$ kHz decoherence: NOT fidelity increases from 99.61% to 99.98% ($\delta\Omega = 0.003$, $\delta\Delta = -2\pi \times 1.55$ MHz, $\delta\phi = -0.040\pi$); Hadamard from 99.46% to 99.92% ($\delta\Omega = -0.052$, $\delta\Delta = -2\pi \times 2.95$ MHz, $\delta\phi = -0.114\pi$). For iSWAP with $g_{12} = 2\pi \times 10$ MHz: fidelity improves from 99.74% to 99.87%. Scheme remains robust under calibration errors up to $\pm 2\pi \times 0.2$ MHz detuning deviation and $\pm 0.02\pi$ phase deviation.
